The repo is not yet under git and has no GitHub remote. DONE WHEN: a cold reader landing on the repo page knows what CoCo Zero is in one paragraph and can find the spec. Not in scope: the spec content itself (CZ-3 onward). [2026-10-21 Repo created and pushed public as github.com/ugufru/coco-zero (user's request). Commits 3644d6c, fdffa23, c75baf0.] [2026-10-25 Closed at the done-when: a cold reader knows what a CoCo Zero is and can find the spec. LICENSE and CONTRIBUTING.md filed as CZ-22. summary: Capture the CoCo Zero vision in the user's own words (docs/vision.md)
description: Every other document derives from this, so it goes first. Interview the user and write docs/vision.md: why CoCo Zero exists, who it is for, what it is not. Established so far from the reference project (~/github/xroar-waveshare-rp2350-pizero (github.com/ugufru/xroar-waveshare-rp2350-pizero)): it began as XRoar on a Waveshare RP2350-PiZero, a CoCo 2 on a 65 x 30 mm board with picture and sound over one digital video cable at 60 fps, USB keyboard and gamepad, microSD; it now also runs a 128 KB CoCo 3; its CLAUDE.md rule 'improvements are on by default, authentic behaviour stays available'; PIZERO-176's 'CoCo Zero is like a little playground for developers, and our limits do not always need to be practical if they are within reach'; units are given away, not sold (docs/kit.md). OPEN QUESTIONS to settle with the user: (1) is CoCo Zero a product, a machine, or a standard any board can meet; (2) does the name cover only RP2350 boards, or also the other XRoar ports in ~/github (Fruit Jam, RP2350-43B, AMOLED, 1.44in LCD HAT); (3) is the cocozero machine profile (CZ-5) the heart of the identity, or the hardware; (4) the document license (e.g. CC BY-SA 4.0) and whether implementations must be open source like XRoar (GPL); (5) the intended audience: builders, developers writing software for it, or both. DONE WHEN: the user has read vision.md and agrees it says what they mean. [2026-10-21 Settled with the user: CoCo Zero is a form factor plus a small feature set, not one board. As every CoCo 2 variant (including the Korean-built ones) shared one motherboard size and case, every CoCo Zero shares the Raspberry Pi Zero board size; the 'Zero' names that size, used by Raspberry Pi, Waveshare, Orange Pi and others. Features: the user named USB-C, mini HDMI and microSD as the ones that stand out and does not want the spec too specific. This answers open questions 1 and 2 (any Pi Zero size board can qualify) and largely 3 (the form factor is the identity; the machine profile is secondary). Still open: 4 (licenses), 5 (audience).] [2026-10-21 Second meaning of 'Zero', from the user: bare metal. Zero operating system in the way, only a lightweight monitor and configuration screen that runs nothing else: just you and the machine, with one layer of software between. Approximated as closely as possible while keeping the essence of operating a CoCo. The user will deepen this later (CZ-18). Also from the user: a CoCo Zero emulates a CoCo 1, 2 or 3 (128K, ideally 512K, 2M and more) (CZ-19), and does extra things the original CoCos never did, a list that will grow (CZ-12). So the vision page has three pillars: the Pi Zero form factor, bare metal, and the CoCo plus extras.] [2026-10-21 The user's model for this repo (2026-10-21): the main documentation is very sparse. It does not tell you how to build a CoCo Zero beyond the general shape. Think of the rules for a kei car or a US mailbox, or a computer case standard: it leaves the most room for DIY builders to adapt it and make it what they want, while letting them depend on third-party manufacturers for the electronics. This is the governing rule for every spec page and belongs at the top of the vision page.] [2026-10-21 The README now states the vision in short form (CZ-1). docs/vision.md may not be needed at all: decide with the user whether the README section is enough.] [2026-10-25 Closed with the user's agreement: the README's 'The vision' section is the vision statement, and docs/vision.md is not being written. Questions 1 to 3 were settled earlier. Remainder filed: question 4 (document license, and whether implementations must be open source) goes to CZ-22 with LICENSE; question 5 (intended audience) is CZ-23.]

summary: What is a CoCo Zero: the one-page definition
description: A short normative page (spec/definition.md) answering 'what is a CoCo Zero' in a paragraph, then its defining traits in a list, then what makes it unique against a real CoCo 2/3, a desktop XRoar, and other retro boards (MiSTer core, CoCoPi, etc.). Drawn from CZ-2. Should be quotable: the paragraph is what goes on a kit card or a forum post. DEPENDS ON CZ-2. [2026-10-21 Framing settled in CZ-2: the definition leads with the form factor (CZ-6) and the feature baseline (CZ-16); the machine profile is secondary.] [2026-10-21 Three pillars to summarise (CZ-2 note): the Pi Zero form factor (CZ-6, CZ-16), bare metal (CZ-18), and a CoCo 1/2/3 plus extras (CZ-19, CZ-12).]

summary: Conformance framework: what qualifies as a CoCo Zero
description: spec/conformance.md: how a device or firmware earns the name. Proposal to test with the user: RFC 2119 requirement levels (MUST / SHOULD / MAY); a short list of MUSTs (the core profile CZ-5, the user-facing interface CZ-7, the hardware baseline CZ-6, open source), and named optional extensions (CZ-14) an implementation declares rather than being judged on. Decide whether there are tiers (for example 'CoCo Zero' and 'CoCo Zero compatible'), and whether a claim is self-certified against the checklist (CZ-10) or reviewed. DEPENDS ON CZ-2, CZ-3. [2026-10-21 Per the sparse-spec model (CZ-2 note): no tiers, no review process, no test suite. A CoCo Zero is anything that meets the requirements in spec/. Keep this page to a few lines, possibly folded into the README or the definition (CZ-3).] [2026-10-25 From CZ-22, still open: does the standard require a CoCo Zero firmware to be open source, or only describe the reference firmware as open (as the README does now)? The documents themselves are CC BY 4.0, which says nothing about implementations. Ask the user.] [2026-10-25 Settled by the user: the firmware of any CoCo Zero must be open source. Added as a requirement to spec/features.md (new Firmware section) and to the README (the Open paragraph and the spec table). The README notes that firmware built on XRoar is open already, since XRoar is GPL 3 or later (~/github/xroar/COPYING.GPL). No license is mandated for implementations beyond being open source.] [2026-10-25 Closed with the user. Conformance is the spec itself: a CoCo Zero is anything that meets every requirement in spec/, with no tiers, no requirement levels, no certification or review. Stated once in the README (top of The standard) and as the opening line of spec/coco-zero-spec.pdf (CZ-24). No spec/conformance.md was written. Its one settled rule, open-source firmware, is in spec/features.md. CZ-10 (checklist and test programs) stays deferred and is probably unneeded.]

summary: Specify the cocozero machine profile
description: The cocozero profile is the one non-canonical machine, decided in the reference project's PIZERO-242 (2026-10-20, in progress there): machine = cocozero | coco2 | coco3, cocozero the default. Today it is a CoCo 2 plus the GIME-style palette and timer registers, the SN76489 sound chip without a cartridge, the 6847t2 font and true lower case; it may take CoCo 3 extras later. coco2 and coco3 are authentic. A profile governs only emulated hardware; host conveniences (key repeat, keycap typing, volume, gamepad mapping, artifact colours) are the same on every machine. DO: spec/machine-cocozero.md, written precisely enough that a second emulator author could implement it and software could detect it: the register addresses and behaviour of each addition, the CPU speeds, memory size, what reads back where on a real CoCo 2 it would not, and how a program detects a CoCo Zero. Source the facts from the reference firmware, not memory. Note: PIZERO-242 is still open, so this spec may lead it; keep the two in step (changes to that project go through its own session). [2026-10-21 The user does not want the standard too specific (CZ-2 note). This stays useful as a description of the reference firmware's default machine, but it is probably informative rather than a requirement. Lowered to medium and off the roadmap.] [2026-10-21 Deferred 2026-10-21: too detailed for the sparse spec the user described (CZ-2 note: like the rules for a kei car or a US mailbox, only the general shape). This is implementation detail, which belongs with an implementation such as the reference firmware, not in the standard. Reopen only if the user asks.]

summary: Form factor: adopt the Raspberry Pi Zero mechanical outline (spec/form-factor.md)
description: The 'Zero' in CoCo Zero is the Raspberry Pi Zero board size, adopted as the CoCo Zero form factor the way every CoCo 2 variant shared one motherboard size (user, 2026-10-21). Source: Raspberry Pi's mechanical drawings, Pi Zero ref RPI-ZERO-V1_2 (2015) and Zero 2 W (same dimensions), at datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rpizero/raspberry-pi-zero-mechanical-drawing.pdf and rpizero2/raspberry-pi-zero-2-w-mechanical-drawing.pdf. Linked, not copied (their drawing; trademark note in the spec). Values: 65 x 30, corner radius 3.0, 4 x M2.5 holes drilled 2.75 +/- 0.05 on a 58 x 23 pattern 3.5 in from each edge; mini HDMI centre x 12.4, micro USB centres 41.4 and 54.0 on the connector edge, microSD at the short edge centre y 16.9, 40-pin header centred x 32.5. Compared with the reference board from ~/github/xroar-waveshare-rp2350-pizero/hardware/case/pizero_case.scad (scaled off Waveshare's drawing, +/- 0.2): outline, insets, HDMI (12.35) and microSD (16.9) match; holes about 3.0; USB-C centres 39.1 and 53.6, so the first USB moves 2.3 mm. [2026-10-21 Drafted spec/form-factor.md: outline and holes required; connector positions a recommendation until the open question is settled.] OPEN: must connector positions be exact enough that every CoCo Zero fits one case (the CoCo 2 analogy says yes), or are outline and holes enough? Also not covered yet: board thickness and height envelope, keep-outs (latched microSD tail), buttons, LED. DONE WHEN: the user agrees the required table and the connector question is decided; the height envelope can be filed as its own issue. [2026-10-21 Connector question decided by the user: every CoCo Zero should fit the same case, but the spec says nothing about connector positions; some cases may need minor modifications, and most will be 3D printed anyway. The user also set the tone: 'it's a spec not a commentary about what you may see on the street.' spec/form-factor.md cut down to the source drawing and the requirements table (outline, corner radius, holes). Removed: the connector table, the comparison with the reference board, and the rationale; the CoCo 2 analogy belongs in the vision page (CZ-2). Height envelope and keep-outs filed as CZ-20. Waiting on the user's read of the page to close.] [2026-10-21 Closed on the user's word. Delivered: spec/form-factor.md, the Pi Zero outline, corner radius and mounting holes from Raspberry Pi's drawing, requirements only. Deliberately not done: connector positions (left out by decision). Remainder: CZ-20 (thickness, height, keep-outs).]

Candidates from the reference project: improvements on by default, authentic behaviour always one setting away and settable per game; everything works on hardware before it is claimed; fully open source in the XRoar tradition; ROMs are the owner's to supply; it plugs into a modern TV with things people already own; a playground for developers, where limits need not be practical if within reach (PIZERO-176). Confirm each with the user. DEPENDS ON CZ-2. [2026-10-21 Bare metal is now a core principle (CZ-18): zero operating system, one layer of software between the user and the machine.] [2026-10-21 The user's model for this repo (2026-10-21): the main documentation is very sparse. summary: Versioning and change process for the standard
description: spec/versioning.md: how the spec is numbered (e.g. 1.0 when CZ-3 to CZ-7 are agreed), what counts as a breaking change, how a change is proposed (an issue here, then a pull request on the public repo), and who decides. Keep it light: one maintainer today.

summary: Beyond the CoCo: the list of things a CoCo Zero does that the original CoCos never did
description: From the user, 2026-10-21: a CoCo Zero does extra things the traditional CoCos never did; that is part of what makes it special, and the list will grow over time. spec/extras.md: each extra with a short name, a one-line description, and whether it is part of the identity (every CoCo Zero has it) or optional (an implementation declares it). Kept light, per the user's wish not to be too specific. Seeded from the reference firmware (~/github/xroar-waveshare-rp2350-pizero README.md): picture and sound over one cable at 60 fps on a modern TV; USB keyboard where each key types what is printed on it, and USB gamepads as joysticks; disks, programs and cartridges picked from on-screen lists off a microSD card; settings per game, and a game that switches the machine to a CoCo 3 by itself; screenshots to the card; a game that starts at power-on (autorun); the CoCo 2 high-speed POKEs with a clean screen; true lower case and a choice of fonts; the GMC's SN76489 sound chip built in; the GIME palette and timer on the CoCo 2 (the cocozero profile, CZ-5); NitrOS-9 boot disks built by a script. Ideas in the reference tracker, not shipped: an MC6845 80-column card (PIZERO-176). Also folds in the earlier 'extensions registry' idea (memory beyond 128K is covered by CZ-19). [2026-10-21 The comparison rows in docs/comparison.md (CZ-15) are a good user-facing statement of these extras: picture, sound, speed, storage, loading, text, keyboard, joysticks, screenshots, settings, size and power, two machines on one board.] [2026-10-21 Per the sparse-spec model (CZ-2 note): this lives in docs/, not spec/. It describes what CoCo Zeros do; it requires nothing.]

summary: Name, logo and trademark guidance

Not legal advice. Ask the user whether a logo or badge exists or is wanted.

The reference pages themselves are a bit out of date; changing them is for that project's session.] [2026-10-25 Closed with the user's agreement. docs/comparison.md is linked from the README twice ('A CoCo, and more' and the CZ-1 images). summary: Feature baseline: what every CoCo Zero board provides
description: spec/features.md. The user named USB-C, mini HDMI and microSD as the features that stand out (2026-10-21), and does not want the standard too specific. Proposed baseline, to confirm with the user, each as MUST unless noted: (1) mini HDMI video, with sound carried in the same cable and no separate audio jack; (2) two USB-C ports, one for power and firmware updates, one USB host port for a keyboard and gamepad (the Pi Zero splits its two micro USB ports the same way); (3) a microSD slot, the machine's disk drive and settings; (4) runs from an ordinary USB-C phone charger and powers the keyboard and gamepad from it; (5) firmware updates over USB-C with no special tools (SHOULD); (6) a reset button reachable in a case (SHOULD); (7) the 40-pin header footprint in the Pi Zero position, populated or not (MAY), which would let a pHAT-size add-on act as a CoCo Zero expansion, the CoCo's cartridge port in this form; (8) a status LED (MAY); (9) open source firmware in the XRoar tradition, ROMs supplied by the owner. Ruled out for now: naming a particular microcontroller (the RP2350 is the reference board's, not a requirement). The spec names the connectors, never their positions (CZ-6). Write it as requirements only, with no commentary (user, 2026-10-21). [2026-10-21 Add from CZ-18: boots straight into the emulated machine, with no operating system; the only other software is the monitor and configuration screen.] [2026-10-21 Per the sparse-spec model (CZ-2 note): cut the list to what defines a CoCo Zero, which the user named: mini HDMI, USB-C, microSD; plus bare metal (CZ-18) and emulating a CoCo (CZ-19). Drop the SHOULD/MAY items (firmware update method, reset button, LED, 40-pin footprint, phone charger power) unless the user wants one; they are builders' choices.] [2026-10-21 User's requirements: support for standard USB-C keyboards; no micro USB or any other USB, USB-C only ('both perfect connector standards'); same for mini HDMI; at least one USB-C port for power and at least one USB-C port hosting USB peripherals; 640p60 output to HDMI with audio; fanless: 'let's keep those linux pis in disguise out of our cases. All CoCo Zeros are passively cooled and quiet.' Drafted spec/features.md with sections Connectors, Video and sound, Performance (CZ-21), Cooling; microSD kept from the user's earlier list. Read 'any other usb' as every USB port on the board being USB-C, and 'same for mini hdmi' as the video output being mini HDMI only (not micro or full-size). Waiting on the user's read.] [2026-10-21 User revised USB: 'just require two USB ports, as we need one for power and programming.' spec/features.md now requires two USB-C ports, one for power and programming, one a USB host for peripherals; the line 'every USB port is USB-C' is gone, so the spec says nothing about further ports.] [2026-10-21 Closed on the user's word. Delivered: spec/features.md Connectors (two USB-C ports, one for power and programming and one USB host; a standard USB-C keyboard works; mini HDMI; microSD), Video and sound (640x480 at 60 Hz over HDMI with sound in the signal) and Cooling (passive, no fan). Deliberately not done: the optional items (reset button, LED, 40-pin footprint, firmware update method). Bare metal and the machines are CZ-18 and CZ-19.]

Explore whether a pinout convention is worth defining (for example a joystick port, a cassette or serial port, a real cartridge bridge), and whether to follow Raspberry Pi's HAT+ conventions (an ID EEPROM). Exploration only: nothing is decided, and the reference board's header use should be checked before proposing pins. [2026-10-21 Deferred 2026-10-21: too detailed for the sparse spec the user described (CZ-2 note: like the rules for a kei car or a US mailbox, only the general shape). This is implementation detail, which belongs with an implementation such as the reference firmware, not in the standard. Reopen only if the user asks.]

summary: Bare metal: zero operating system, one layer of software between you and the machine
description: The second meaning of 'Zero', from the user 2026-10-21: there is zero operating system to get in the way. Just a lightweight monitor and configuration screen that does not run anything else; just you and the machine, with one layer of software between. The CoCo Zero approximates that as closely as possible while keeping the essence of what it means to operate a CoCo. The user wants to deepen this idea later, so this issue starts by writing down what was said (docs/bare-metal.md or a section of the vision page) and collecting questions for that conversation, for example: what the monitor and configuration screen may and may not do; whether it counts as part of the 'one layer'; whether a real-time library or SDK (the reference uses the arduino-pico core) is acceptable where an OS is not; what 'the essence of operating a CoCo' requires (power on to BASIC in seconds, nothing to log in to, nothing to shut down?). Implication already noted: Linux-class Zero size boards qualify only with bare-metal firmware (CZ-9).

summary: Machines and memory: a CoCo 1, 2 or 3, from 128K up to 512K, 2M and more
description: From the user, 2026-10-21: a CoCo Zero emulates a CoCo 1, 2 or 3; the CoCo 3 at 128K, but ideally 512K, 2M and more. spec/machines.md. To settle: whether an implementation must offer all three machines or at least one (the reference firmware does the CoCo 2 and a 128K CoCo 3, and a CoCo 1 is close to a CoCo 2 with the older ROMs); whether 128K is the floor and 512K the recommendation; how memory beyond 512K is described, since 2M CoCo 3 upgrades are third-party designs and need a named model to emulate. Reference facts: the RP2350-PiZero has 520 KB SRAM and no PSRAM fitted, which is why the reference stops at 128K; fitting PSRAM is under discussion with Waveshare (reference docs/supplier-primer.md, PIZERO-243). Keep each machine's description short; the cocozero profile (CZ-5) is a machine variant and belongs here as a link. [2026-10-21 Per the sparse-spec model (CZ-2 note): a few lines naming the machines and memory sizes, not a description of each machine.] [2026-10-25 Settled by the user: a 128K CoCo 3 is the minimum implementation; 64K is the minimum configuration for a CoCo 1 or 2. Read as: every CoCo Zero emulates a CoCo 3 with at least 128K, and a CoCo 1 or 2 is optional but has at least 64K when offered. Written as spec/machines.md (two requirements, nothing else) and added to the README spec table; the README vision line now reads 'at least a 128K CoCo 3, and ideally 512K, 2M or more. It can be a 64K CoCo 1 or 2 as well.' Deliberately not in the spec: 512K and 2M stay as the README's 'ideally', not a recommendation level, since spec pages carry requirements only (CZ-6); which 2M upgrade model to emulate is left to the builder. The cocozero profile (CZ-5, deferred) is not linked yet. Waiting on the user's read.] [2026-10-25 Closed: the user read spec/machines.md and the README changes and approved them.]

description: Remainder of CZ-6. A case also needs to know how thick the board is and how tall its parts stand above and below it, and what space must stay clear (for example the tail of a latched microSD card, which stands 3.90 mm out of the housing on the reference board per ~/github/xroar-waveshare-rp2350-pizero/hardware/case/README.md). Decide with the user whether any of this belongs in the spec at all: CZ-6 settled that the spec carries only what is required and no commentary, and left connector positions out entirely. If something goes in, it is a hard limit, for example a maximum height that the reference case accommodates (18.6 mm overall case height; PCB thickness 1.6 marked unconfirmed in pizero_case.scad). Buttons and the status LED belong to CZ-16, not here. [2026-10-21 The kei car and mailbox model (CZ-2 note) does have size limits, so a maximum height may fit the spec if the user wants one; nothing else here does.]

summary: Performance minimums: double speed, 60 Hz, 640x480
description: From the user 2026-10-21: performance specs belong in the standard, for example 'a CoCo Zero should be able to clock double speed at 60hz at 640x480 resolution. stuff like that.' Like the size limits in a kei car rule, these are hard numbers a builder must meet, not advice on how. spec/performance.md (or a section of spec/features.md if it stays short). Requirement as stated: real-time emulation at double speed (the 6809 at about 1.79 MHz: the CoCo 3's fast mode, the CoCo 2's POKE 65497,0) while putting out 640x480 at 60 Hz. Reference facts (~/github/xroar-waveshare-rp2350-pizero README.md, Performance): the reference meets this on an RP2350 at 252 MHz, standard 640x480p60 (25.2 MHz pixel, 800x525), a locked 60 fps; as a CoCo 3 at 1.79 MHz at most 15.2 ms of the 16.67 ms frame; the CoCo 2's POKE 65497,0 about 12.6 ms. Candidates to put to the user, each a number not a method: no dropped or repeated frames; sound with no gaps; power-on to the BASIC prompt within a few seconds; keyboard and gamepad input within a frame or two. Keep to the few the user accepts. Wording to settle: 'double speed' measured as the emulated CPU clock, and whether 60 Hz means the video output, the emulated machine's frame rate, or both (the reference does both). [2026-10-21 User's answers: quick power-on, yes; no dropped frames and no sound gaps, yes; '640p60 output to hdmi with audio', so 60 Hz means the HDMI output. Input latency was not taken up, so dropped. Drafted as the Performance section of spec/features.md (short enough not to need its own page). OPEN: the number of seconds for power-on to BASIC (left as N; the reference README says the OK prompt appears 'after a few seconds').] [2026-10-21 User: 'let's not specify how long.' No time limit. spec/features.md now says 'Power-on goes straight to the BASIC prompt', keeping the quick power-on the user wanted without a number. No open questions left; waiting on the user's read of the page.] [2026-10-21 Closed on the user's word. Delivered: the Performance section of spec/features.md: real time at double speed (about 1.79 MHz), no dropped frames, no gaps in the sound, power-on straight to the BASIC prompt. Deliberately not done: a time limit for power-on and an input latency figure, both declined by the user.]

description: From the user, 2026-10-25: provide a one-page PDF as an alternative to the website. No fluff, just the spec. summary: HDMI names only the connector and cable; the signal is DVI with embedded audio
description: From the user, 2026-10-25: HDMI is a licensed term the project cannot afford. A CoCo Zero does not produce HDMI signals: the signal is DVI with embedded audio. The physical connector and cable are mini HDMI, and the standard calls them that, because that is what people buy cables and adapters by; HDMI is not used for anything else. (The formal connector name, HDMI Type C, is the same trademark, and no neutral standard name exists, so it was dropped rather than replaced.) Changed: spec/features.md (connector line now 'a mini HDMI connector'; video section now '640 x 480 at 60 Hz, as a DVI signal' and 'Sound is embedded in the DVI signal'), the README spec table ('DVI with embedded sound'), and the regenerated spec/coco-zero-spec.pdf. Left as they are, since they name the connector or cable: the README image alt texts (mini HDMI cable, adapter, port) and the Mini HDMI tile in docs/images/coco-and-more.svg. Not changed: historical notes in issues.jsonl and past commits. The reference project made a similar call (its PIZERO-174) and is that project's business.
